sentences.text:
Heard Mahendra Pratap Singh, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Sri Rahul Singh,
learned Standing Counsel appearing for the State and Sri Subham Tripathi, learned counsel appearing for K.G.M.U., who tenders the medical report (hearing impairment) regarding physical disability of the petitioner in a sealed cover, which has been opened by the Court.
2. On the last date of hearing of this petition, this Court on 17.04.2023 passed the following order:-
"1. Heard Sri Mahendra Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Rahul Kumar Singh, learned Standing Counsel.
2. In compliance of the order dated 13.4.2023 passed by this Court, Sri Manoj Agarwal, Chief Medical Officer, Lucknow is present in person.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed being aggrieved by the order dated 9.1.2023 passed by the Chief Medical Officer,
Lucknow, whereby he directed the petitioner to get himself examined by a medical board of the King George Medical University, Lucknow (for short ?KGMU?) in respect of his physical disability (hearing impairment).
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been examined for his physical disability i.e. hearing impairment for five times in the government institutions.

He further submits that when the five times the petitioner has been found to be physically handicapped under the provisions of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, there is no ground to send the petitioner time and again to get the fresh certificate for his physical disability.

entities.text: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He also submits that this procedure of sending the petitioner time and again to get himself examined for his physical disability, is against Rule 18(2) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2017 (for short ?Rules, 2017?).

entities.text: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2017
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
He, therefore, submits that the impugned order passed by the Chief Medical Officer, Lucknow is against the statutory prescription and it is nothing but harassment of the petitioner, who is being subjected to medical examination time and again for his physical disability.
5.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that since under the Rules,
2017, a physically handicapped person has to be examined only once and the government institutions have issued physical disability certificate in favour of the petitioner, the exercise to send petitioner time and again for his physical disability, is neither desirable nor is as per the law.
6.

On the other hand, Sri Rahul Kumar Singh, learned Standing Counsel has submitted that the petitioner's record in respect of his physical disability (hearing impairment) is missing from his service record.
Twice the petitioner had produced the report himself and it was not received through proper channel in a sealed cover.

He further submits that on 7.10.2022 when the petitioner went for the medical examination, he sent someone-else in place of himself, for which FIR No.0297 of 2022, under Sections 419 and 420 IPC came to be registered by the members of the medical board.

He, therefore, submits that to find out veracity of the physical disability condition/certificate of the petitioner, the Chef Medical Officer, Lucknow has directed his extermination by the bigger medical board and such proceedings are to be video graphed.

He further submits that the petitioner in any manner is not prejudiced by the said exercise and if he is physically handicapped (hearing impairment), he has nothing to fear and, the examination by the bigger medical board would clear the dust/cloud in respect of the physical disability of the petitioner.
7. I have considered the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 8. When there is doubt in respect to the physical disability of the petitioner inasmuch as the record as stated is issuing and, twice the reports were produced without proper channel and, once the FIR came to be registered, it would be appropriate to get the petitioner examined.
As such, I do not find that the impugned order suffers from any illegality or it is unjust or improper.
Once the petitioner appears and examined, it would clear the dust and cloud over his physical disability certificate.

9. In view thereof, the Vice-Chancellor, KGMU, Lucknow is directed to constitute a medical board of three eminent ENT specialists to examine the petitioner in respect of his physical disability (hearing impairment) and submit a report to this Court through Sri Shubham Tripathi, counsel who represents the KGMU, Lucknow by the next date of listing of this petition.

10. The petitioner is directed to appear before the Registrar of the KGMU, Lucknow on 19.4.2023 at 10.30 AM to get himself examined medically in respect of his physical disability (hearing impairment) along with Aadhar Card.
Voter Identity Card and the Departmental Identity Card to show the proof of identity.

It is made clear that if the petitioner is adjudged as physically handicapped by the medical board so constituted for examination of the petitioner, no further examination of the petitioner shall be carried out thorough out his service career and this certificate will hold good for all times to come.

11. Sri Rahul Kumar Singh, learned Standing Counsel will communicate the order passed today to Sri Shubham Tripathi, who will forward it to the Vice-Chancellor,
KGMU, Lucknow for necessary compliance.
12. List this petition on 21.4.2023 peremptorily, on which date the report should be produced by Sri Shubham Tripathi, learned counsel representing the KGMU,
Lucknow in a sealed cover.
13. On the next date, the Chief Medical Officer, Lucknow shall also remain present."
3.

In compliance of the said order, K.G.M.U. administration constituted four members Medical Board consisting of (i) Chief Medical Officer, Gandhi Memorial and Associated Hospital, K.G.M.U.,
Lucknow, (Chairman); (ii) Dr. Veerendra Verma, Professor, Department of Otorhinolaryngology (Member); (iii) Dr. H.P. Singh, Additional Professor, Department of Otorhinolaryngology (Member); and (iv) Dr Manish Chandra, Associate Professor, Department of Otorhinolaryngology (Member) who has assessed the petitioner regarding his physical disability (hearing impairment)
and the medical board, so constituted, by the order of this Court has assessed the percentage of hearing disability of the petitioner as 70.4 %.

entities.text: Gandhi Memorial and Associated Hospital, K.G.M.U.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Said medical report is taken on record.
4. Manoj Agarwal, Chief Medical Officer, Lucknow is present in the Court.

He has submitted that he will issue physical disability certificate to the petitioner considering the medical board report, so constituted, as per the direction of this Court in its order dated 17.04.2023, and no further Sanjay Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. ... on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156152889/
3

examination of the petitioner in future shall take place.
5. Photocopy of the said report has been taken on record and original copy has been issued to the Chief Medical Officer for issuing necessary directions within a period of a week.
6.
With the aforesaid direction, the petition stands finally disposed of.
